title: The kid who copies it
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: A kid at the laundromat is copying the digest's dog onto the back of a real-estate flyer. Badly. Wood watches over his shoulder and does not correct him. The strip draws the kid's dog and it's the strip's dog.

panels.composition: The laundromat. A KID of nine at the folding table copying the digest's dog onto the back of a flyer with a pencil. Tongue out.

image.prompt: a nine-year-old at a laundromat folding table copying a cartoon dog from a booklet onto the back of a flyer with a pencil, tongue out, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The kid's dog: four strokes, wrong, alive.

image.prompt: close on a child's pencil drawing of a small dog, crude and lively, black and white, no words

panels.composition: WOOD behind him. Not correcting. BARNABY looking at the drawing of himself.

image.prompt: a young man standing behind a child at a table, watching without interfering, a small dog looking at the drawing, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The strip's own last panel: the kid's dog, redrawn exactly, as the strip's dog. Four strokes, wrong, alive.

image.prompt: close on a comic panel containing a crude child-style drawing of a small dog, black and white, no words
image.notes: The kid's drawing reproduced as the strip's panel. Wrong and alive.

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The kid's dog becomes the strip's dog for one panel. Not corrected.
